source: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, grouped into checks a tester can run. Descriptions are ours.

heuristics.name: Text alternatives
heuristics.description: Images, icons and icon-only buttons need a text name for screen reader users.
heuristics.apply: Check that every image and icon button has a meaningful accessible name, not a file name or nothing.

heuristics.name: Keyboard only
heuristics.description: Everything must work without a mouse, with no place where keyboard focus gets stuck.
heuristics.apply: Do each main task using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, the arrow keys and Escape.

heuristics.name: Visible focus
heuristics.description: The keyboard focus should always be visible, and move in a sensible order.
heuristics.apply: Tab through each page and check you can always see where the focus is and that its order makes sense.

heuristics.name: Colour contrast
heuristics.description: Text needs enough contrast with its background to be readable.
heuristics.apply: Check text and important icons against their background, especially greyed-out, placeholder and small text.

heuristics.name: Not colour alone
heuristics.description: Meaning shouldn't be carried by colour only, such as a red border for an error.
heuristics.apply: Look for states shown only by colour, and check there's also text or an icon.

heuristics.name: Form labels
heuristics.description: Every input needs a label that stays visible and is tied to the field, not just placeholder text.
heuristics.apply: Check each field has a visible label and that its accessible name matches it.

heuristics.name: Error identification
heuristics.description: Input errors must be described in text, next to the field, and announced to assistive technology.
heuristics.apply: Cause an input error and check the message is in text, tied to the field and not only a colour change.

heuristics.name: Zoom and reflow
heuristics.description: Pages must stay usable at 200% zoom and on a narrow screen, without horizontal scrolling.
heuristics.apply: Zoom to 200% and narrow the window to phone width, then do a main task.

heuristics.name: Page structure
heuristics.description: Headings, landmarks and a page title let assistive technology users find their way.
heuristics.apply: Check each page has a meaningful title, one main heading and headings that describe its sections.

heuristics.name: Dialog focus
heuristics.description: When a dialog opens, focus should move into it, stay in it and return when it closes.
heuristics.apply: Open each dialog with the keyboard, tab around inside it, close it with Escape and check where the focus lands.

heuristics.name: Adjustable timing
heuristics.description: Time limits and moving content should be avoidable, pausable or long enough.
heuristics.apply: Look for timeouts, auto-advancing content and messages that vanish before they can be read.

heuristics.name: Status messages
heuristics.description: Messages that appear without a page change (saved, added to cart) should be announced to screen readers.
heuristics.apply: Trigger a status message and check it's in a live region or otherwise exposed to assistive technology.

heuristics.name: Language of the page
heuristics.description: The page should declare its language, and switch it when the user changes language.
heuristics.apply: Check the page's lang attribute, then change the language and check it again.
